subject: Retention & erasure evidence request — default logs and exceptional captures
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Default capture/retention evidence and erasure proof

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. We need a concise written response for our internal audit: 1) what Redwood keeps by default for a standard hosted inference request (we're focusing on request text, model outputs, streaming fragments, KV cache artifacts, and attachments); 2) the default retention window for each item; and 3) what evidence you can provide if BrightBank requests a tenant-scoped erasure (audit trail, deletion marker, hashes, or export showing removal).

A couple of specifics we care about:
- If a user sends a file as part of a request (attachment), is that preserved by default?
- For streaming responses where tokens are flushed incrementally, are intermediate fragments retained anywhere beyond the final assembled output?
- Are cached KV entries used for repeated prompts ever written to persistent storage that survives an erasure request?

Would you be able to send an example erasure report showing the artifacts that would be generated for a BrightBank erasure request (we're not asking for real customer data — a synthetic run with identifiers is fine)? We need this for our security questionnaire and upcoming compliance review on Aug 12.

Best,
Michael Sloan
Senior InfoSec Analyst
BrightBank

Attachment: security_questionnaire_template.xlsx (referenced, not included)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Default capture/retention evidence and erasure proof

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list. I can provide the responses and a synthetic erasure report. High level answers below; I will follow with a short synthetic report and runbook links by EOD tomorrow.

Quick answers (summary):
- Default capture: we record the raw request payload (user-provided prompt and any attached file metadata), the model's final generated outputs (finalized answer), and system-level request metadata (timestamps, model id, route).
- Streaming fragments: streaming buffer fragments are not persisted as separate artifacts in long term storage by default. Only the final assembled response is stored when the request qualifies as an archived artifact.
- KV cache: in the hosted offering KV caches used for serving are kept in ephemeral in-memory caches and local SSD-backed caches which are rotated; by default those caches are not persisted into long-term customer-visible blob storage and are erased as part of standard TTL processes.
- Attachments: attachments provided with a request are retained only if the customer has enabled artifact persistence for file uploads; otherwise we keep attachment metadata (filename, size, mime) and transient storage used during processing which is purged within the default TTL.

I need to loop in Ben for the erasure evidence artifacts and ask Kim for the official runbook link and recommended wording for the synthetic erasure report for your auditors.

Regards,
Marissa
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

I also made two clarifications you should include in the external note: (1) cached KV entries are ephemeral and not copied to long-term object stores by default (we'll explicitly note exceptions for Dedicated customers with custom snapshotting enabled), and (2) streaming fragments are only kept beyond transient buffers if a customer opts into transcript capture.

Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBFy-example-runbook

Blurb to paste to customer: 
"Redwood tenant-scoped erasure is performed via an automated pipeline that scans our metadata index for a tenant identifier, marks matching artifacts with a deletion marker, initiates object store deletes for persisted blobs, and emits a downloadable erasure manifest. Audit events (timestamped) are written to the control-plane audit log. Typical completion time for the hosted product is within 48 hours for the metadata and deletion markers; blob removal from object storage may depend on the underlying provider's eventual consistency and can take up to 7 days in edge cases. For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide equivalent APIs and can produce tailored evidence packages on request."

I've attached a short synthetic erasure report (placeholder) and a text file with the public KB link you can include in inline replies.

Hi Michael — attaching a synthetic erasure report and our retention/runbook links as requested. Summary below (please paste into your questionnaire as needed).

Summary (concise):
- What we capture by default:
  * Request payload (prompt text and request metadata).
  * Final model output (finalized, assembled answer).
  * System metadata (model id, timestamps, request route).
  * Attachment metadata; attachments only persisted as blobs when artifact persistence is enabled.

- Retention windows (defaults):
  * Request payload & final outputs: 45 days by default for hosted API unless customer configures a different policy.
  * Attachment blobs: transient during processing; persisted only if customer enables artifact persistence — otherwise removed within 7 days.
  * Streaming fragments: not persisted separately by default; only final assembled output retained.
  * KV caches: ephemeral and cleared under normal TTL; not written to long-term blob storage by default (exceptions: Dedicated snapshotting).

- Evidence produced for tenant-scoped erasure:
  * Deletion manifest (list of deleted artifact ids, timestamps).
  * Deletion markers written to metadata index (with deletion timestamp).
  * Control-plane audit events (timestamped) and an exportable audit log segment.
  * SHA256 placeholders in the synthetic report for removed blobs (we do not publish hashes of real customer content).

Attachments included: synthetic erasure report (erasure_report_BrightBank_2026-08-04.pdf) and a runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBFy-example-runbook (public excerpt available at https://redwood.example.com/kb/retention-defaults).

If you need the report expanded into a CSV manifest or a signed statement for your compliance package, let us know and we can schedule a short call with Kim and Ben to walk a reviewer through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
